qt: to the Commission Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2026/13881 exempts Category 1 new genomic technique (NGT) plants, which remain genetically modified organisms (GMOs), from most EU GMO requirements. Under Article 4 of the regulation, a positive verification decision pursuant to Article 6 or 7 is a prerequisite for the deliberate release or placing on the market of such plants under the Category 1 regime. No subsequent GMO-specific authorisation is generally required. Article 6 bis of the Aarhus Convention requires early and effective public participation in decisions on whether to permit the deliberate release or placing on the market of GMOs. However, the NGT verification procedures do not explicitly provide for such participation. The Commission is therefore asked: 1.
Does it consider verification decisions under Articles 6 and 7 of the regulation to fall within the scope of Article 6 bis of the Aarhus Convention? If not, on what legal grounds?
How does the Commission ensure compliance with the public participation requirements laid down in Article 6 bis of and Annex I bis to the Convention?

Given the procedural deadlines, how can effective public participation be ensured in national verification procedures under Article 6 of the regulation, and what discretion do Member States have to introduce additional participation requirements?

Regulation (EU) 2026/1388 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2026 on plants obtained by certain new genomic techniques and their products, and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/625, OJ L, 2026/1388, 26.6.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1388/oj. 1
